title: अंश १ · अध्याय ४

items.speaker: श्रीमैत्रेय उवाच
items.text:
ब्रह्मानारायणाख्योऽसौ कल्पादौ भगवान्यथा ।
ससर्ज सर्वभूतानि तदाचक्ष्व महामुने ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
brahmānārāyaṇākhyo'sau kalpādau bhagavānyathā |
sasarja sarvabhūtāni tadācakṣva mahāmune || 1 ||

items.speaker: श्रीपराशर उवाच
items.text:
प्रजाः ससर्ज भगवान्ब्रह्मा नारायणात्मकः ।
प्रजापतिपतिर्देवो यथा तन्मे निशामय ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
prajāḥ sasarja bhagavānbrahmā nārāyaṇātmakaḥ |
prajāpatipatirdevo yathā tanme niśāmaya || 2 ||

items.text:
अतीतकल्पावसाने निशासुप्तोत्थितः प्रभुः ।
सत्त्वोद्रि क्तस्तथा ब्रह्मा शून्यं लोकमवैक्षत ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
atītakalpāvasāne niśāsuptotthitaḥ prabhuḥ |
sattvodri ktastathā brahmā śūnyaṃ lokamavaikṣata || 3 ||

items.text:
नारायणः परोऽचिन्त्यः परोषामपि स प्रभुः ।
ब्रह्मस्वरूपी भगवाननादिः सर्वसम्भवः ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
nārāyaṇaḥ paro'cintyaḥ paroṣāmapi sa prabhuḥ |
brahmasvarūpī bhagavānanādiḥ sarvasambhavaḥ || 4 ||

items.text:
इमं चोदाहरन्त्यत्र श्लोकं नारायणं प्रति ।
ब्रह्मस्वरूपिणं देवं जगतः प्रभवाप्ययम् ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
imaṃ codāharantyatra ślokaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prati |
brahmasvarūpiṇaṃ devaṃ jagataḥ prabhavāpyayam || 5 ||

items.text:
आपो नारा इति प्रोक्ता आपो वै नरसूनवः ।
अयनं तस्य ताः पूर्वं तेन नारायणः स्मृतः ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
āpo nārā iti proktā āpo vai narasūnavaḥ |
ayanaṃ tasya tāḥ pūrvaṃ tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ || 6 ||

items.text:
तोयान्तःस्थां महीं ज्ञात्वा जगत्येकार्णवीकृते ।
अनुमानात्तदुद्धारं कर्तुकामः प्रजापतिः ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
toyāntaḥsthāṃ mahīṃ jñātvā jagatyekārṇavīkṛte |
anumānāttaduddhāraṃ kartukāmaḥ prajāpatiḥ || 7 ||

items.text:
अकरोत्स्वतनूमन्यां कल्पादिषु यथा पुरा ।
सत्स्यकूर्मादिकां तद्वद्वाराहं वरुरास्थितः ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
akarotsvatanūmanyāṃ kalpādiṣu yathā purā |
satsyakūrmādikāṃ tadvadvārāhaṃ varurāsthitaḥ || 8 ||

items.text:
वेदयज्ञमयं रूपमश्षोजगतः स्थितौ ।
स्थितः स्थिरात्मा सर्वात्मा परमात्मा प्रजापतिः ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
vedayajñamayaṃ rūpamaśṣojagataḥ sthitau |
sthitaḥ sthirātmā sarvātmā paramātmā prajāpatiḥ || 9 ||

items.text:
जनलोकगतैस्सिद्धैस्सनकाद्यैरभिष्टुतः ।
प्रविवेश तदा तोयमात्माधारो धराधरः ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
janalokagataissiddhaissanakādyairabhiṣṭutaḥ |
praviveśa tadā toyamātmādhāro dharādharaḥ || 10 ||

items.text:
निरीक्ष्य तं तदा देवी पातालातलमागतम् ।
तुष्टाव प्रणता भूत्वा भक्तिनम्रा वसुन्धरा ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
nirīkṣya taṃ tadā devī pātālātalamāgatam |
tuṣṭāva praṇatā bhūtvā bhaktinamrā vasundharā || 11 ||

items.text:
नमस्ते पुण्डरीकाक्ष शंखचक्रगदाधर ।
मामुद्धरास्मादद्य त्वं त्वत्तोऽहं पूर्वमुत्थिता ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
namaste puṇḍarīkākṣa śaṃkhacakragadādhara |
māmuddharāsmādadya tvaṃ tvatto'haṃ pūrvamutthitā || 12 ||
items.speaker: श्रीपृथिव्युवाच

items.text:
त्वयाहमुद्धृता पूर्वं त्वन्मयाहं जनार्दन ।
तथान्यानि च भूतानि गगनादीन्यश्षोतः ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
tvayāhamuddhṛtā pūrvaṃ tvanmayāhaṃ janārdana |
tathānyāni ca bhūtāni gaganādīnyaśṣotaḥ || 13 ||

items.text:
नमस्ते परमात्मात्मन्पुरुषात्मन्नमोस्तु ते ।
प्रधानव्यक्तभूताय कालभूताय ते नमः ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
namaste paramātmātmanpuruṣātmannamostu te |
pradhānavyaktabhūtāya kālabhūtāya te namaḥ || 14 ||

items.text:
त्वं कर्ता सर्वभूतानां त्वं पाता त्वं विनाशकृत् ।
सर्गादिषु प्रभो ब्रह्मविष्णुरुद्रा त्मरूपधृक् ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
tvaṃ kartā sarvabhūtānāṃ tvaṃ pātā tvaṃ vināśakṛt |
sargādiṣu prabho brahmaviṣṇurudrā tmarūpadhṛk || 15 ||

items.text:
सम्भक्षयित्वा सकलं जगत्येकार्णवीकृते ।
श्षोए! त्वमेव गोविंद चिन्त्यमानो मनीषिभिः ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
sambhakṣayitvā sakalaṃ jagatyekārṇavīkṛte |
śṣoe! tvameva goviṃda cintyamāno manīṣibhiḥ || 16 ||

items.text:
भवतो यत्परं तत्त्वं तन्न जानाति कश्चन ।
अवतारेषु यद्रू पं तदर्चन्ति दिवौकसः ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
bhavato yatparaṃ tattvaṃ tanna jānāti kaścana |
avatāreṣu yadrū paṃ tadarcanti divaukasaḥ || 17 ||

items.text:
त्वामाराध्य परं ब्रह्म याता मुक्तिं मुमुक्षवः ।
वासुदेवमनाराध्य को मोक्षं समवाप्स्यति ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
tvāmārādhya paraṃ brahma yātā muktiṃ mumukṣavaḥ |
vāsudevamanārādhya ko mokṣaṃ samavāpsyati || 18 ||

items.text:
यत्किंचिन्मनसा ग्राह्यं यद्ग्राह्यं चक्षुरादिभिः ।
बुद्ध्या च यत्परिच्छेद्यं तद्रू पमखिलं तव ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr:
yatkiṃcinmanasā grāhyaṃ yadgrāhyaṃ cakṣurādibhiḥ |
buddhyā ca yatparicchedyaṃ tadrū pamakhilaṃ tava || 19 ||

items.text:
त्वन्मयाहं त्वदाधारा त्वत्सृष्टा त्वत्समाश्रया ।
माधवीमिति लोकोयमभिधत्ते ततो हि माम् ॥ २० ॥
items.tr:
tvanmayāhaṃ tvadādhārā tvatsṛṣṭā tvatsamāśrayā |
mādhavīmiti lokoyamabhidhatte tato hi mām || 20 ||

items.text:
जयाखिलज्ञानमय जय स्थूलमयाव्यय ।
जयाऽनन्त जयाव्यक्त जय व्यक्तमय प्रभो ॥ २१ ॥
items.tr:
jayākhilajñānamaya jaya sthūlamayāvyaya |
jayā'nanta jayāvyakta jaya vyaktamaya prabho || 21 ||

items.text:
परापरात्मन्विश्वात्मञ्जय यज्ञपतेऽनघ ।
त्वं यज्ञस्त्वं वषट्कारस्त्वमॐकारस्त्वमग्नयः ॥ २२ ॥
items.tr:
parāparātmanviśvātmañjaya yajñapate'nagha |
tvaṃ yajñastvaṃ vaṣaṭkārastvamaoṃkārastvamagnayaḥ || 22 ||

items.text:
त्वं वेदास्त्वं तदङ्गानि त्वं यज्ञपुरुषो हरे ।
सूर्यादयो ग्रहास्तारा नक्षत्राण्यखितं जगत् ॥ २३ ॥
items.tr:
tvaṃ vedāstvaṃ tadaṅgāni tvaṃ yajñapuruṣo hare |
sūryādayo grahāstārā nakṣatrāṇyakhitaṃ jagat || 23 ||

items.text:
मूर्तामूर्तमदृश्यं च दृश्यं च पुरुषोत्तम ।
यच्चोक्तं यच्च नैवोक्तं मयात्र परमेश्वर ।
तत्सर्वं त्वं नमस्तुभ्यं भूयोभूयो नमोनमः ॥ २४ ॥
items.tr:
mūrtāmūrtamadṛśyaṃ ca dṛśyaṃ ca puruṣottama |
yaccoktaṃ yacca naivoktaṃ mayātra parameśvara |
tatsarvaṃ tvaṃ namastubhyaṃ bhūyobhūyo namonamaḥ || 24 ||

items.speaker: श्रीपराशर उवाच
items.text:
एवं संस्तूयमानस्तु पृथिव्या धरणीधरः ।
सामस्वरध्वनिः श्रीमाञ् जगर्ज परिघर्घरम् ॥ २५ ॥
items.tr:
evaṃ saṃstūyamānastu pṛthivyā dharaṇīdharaḥ |
sāmasvaradhvaniḥ śrīmāñ jagarja parighargharam || 25 ||

items.text:
ततः समुत्क्षिप्य धरां स्वदंष्ट्रया महावराहः स्फुटपद्मलोचनः ।
रसातलादुत्पलपत्रसन्निभः समुत्थितो नील इवाचलो महान् ॥ २६ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ samutkṣipya dharāṃ svadaṃṣṭrayā mahāvarāhaḥ sphuṭapadmalocanaḥ |
rasātalādutpalapatrasannibhaḥ samutthito nīla ivācalo mahān || 26 ||

items.text:
उत्तिष्ठता तेन मुखानिलाहतं तत्संभवाम्भो जनलोकसंश्रयान् ।
प्रक्षालयामास हि तान्महाद्युतीन् सनान्दनादीनपकल्मषान् मुनीन् ॥ २७ ॥
items.tr:
uttiṣṭhatā tena mukhānilāhataṃ tatsaṃbhavāmbho janalokasaṃśrayān |
prakṣālayāmāsa hi tānmahādyutīn sanāndanādīnapakalmaṣān munīn || 27 ||

items.text:
प्रयान्ति तोयानि खुराग्रविक्षतरसातलेऽधः कृतशब्दसन्तति ।
श्वासानिलास्ताः परितः प्रयांति सिद्धा जने ये नियता वसन्ति ॥ २८ ॥
items.tr:
prayānti toyāni khurāgravikṣatarasātale'dhaḥ kṛtaśabdasantati |
śvāsānilāstāḥ paritaḥ prayāṃti siddhā jane ye niyatā vasanti || 28 ||

items.text:
उत्तिष्ठतस्तस्य जलार्द्र कुक्षेर्महावराहस्य महीं विगृह्य ।
विधुन्वतो वेदमयं शरीरं रोमान्तरस्था मुनयः स्तुवन्ति ॥ २९ ॥
items.tr:
uttiṣṭhatastasya jalārdra kukṣermahāvarāhasya mahīṃ vigṛhya |
vidhunvato vedamayaṃ śarīraṃ romāntarasthā munayaḥ stuvanti || 29 ||

items.text:
तं तुष्टुवुस्तोषपरीतचेतसो लोके जने ये निवसन्ति योगिनः ।
सनन्दनाद्या ह्यतिनम्रकन्धरा धराधरं धीरतरोद्धतेक्षणम् ॥ ३० ॥
items.tr:
taṃ tuṣṭuvustoṣaparītacetaso loke jane ye nivasanti yoginaḥ |
sanandanādyā hyatinamrakandharā dharādharaṃ dhīrataroddhatekṣaṇam || 30 ||

items.text:
जयेश्वराणां परमेश केशव प्रभो गदाशंखधरासिचक्रधृक् ।
प्रसूतिनाशस्थितिहेतुरीश्वरस्त्वमेव नान्यत्परमं च यत्पदम् ॥ ३१ ॥
items.tr:
jayeśvarāṇāṃ parameśa keśava prabho gadāśaṃkhadharāsicakradhṛk |
prasūtināśasthitiheturīśvarastvameva nānyatparamaṃ ca yatpadam || 31 ||

items.text:
पादेषु वेदास्तव यूपदंष्ट्रा दन्तेषु जज्ञाश्चितयश्च वक्त्रे ।
हुताशजिह्वोसि तनूरुहाणि दर्भाः प्रभो यज्ञपुमांस्त्वमेव ॥ ३२ ॥
items.tr:
pādeṣu vedāstava yūpadaṃṣṭrā danteṣu jajñāścitayaśca vaktre |
hutāśajihvosi tanūruhāṇi darbhāḥ prabho yajñapumāṃstvameva || 32 ||

items.text:
विलोचने रात्र्! यहनी महात्मन्सर्वाश्रयं ब्रह्मपरं शिरस्ते ।
सूक्तान्यश्षोआ!णि सटाकलापो घ्राणं समस्तानि हवींषि देव ॥ ३३ ॥
items.tr:
vilocane rātr! yahanī mahātmansarvāśrayaṃ brahmaparaṃ śiraste |
sūktānyaśṣoā!ṇi saṭākalāpo ghrāṇaṃ samastāni havīṃṣi deva || 33 ||

items.text:
स्रुक्तुण्डसामस्वरधीरनादप्राग्वंशकायाखिलसत्रसन्धे ।
पूर्तेष्टधर्मश्रवणोसि देव सनातनात्मन्भगवन्प्रसीद ॥ ३४ ॥
items.tr:
sruktuṇḍasāmasvaradhīranādaprāgvaṃśakāyākhilasatrasandhe |
pūrteṣṭadharmaśravaṇosi deva sanātanātmanbhagavanprasīda || 34 ||

items.text:
पदक्रमाक्रान्तभुवं भवन्तमादिस्थितं चाक्षरविश्वमूर्ते ।
विश्वस्य विद्मः परमेश्वरोऽसि प्रसीद नाथोसि परावरस्य ॥ ३५ ॥
items.tr:
padakramākrāntabhuvaṃ bhavantamādisthitaṃ cākṣaraviśvamūrte |
viśvasya vidmaḥ parameśvaro'si prasīda nāthosi parāvarasya || 35 ||

items.text:
दंष्ट्राग्रविन्यस्तमश्षोमेतद्भूमण्डलं नाथ विभाव्यते ते ।
विगाहतः पद्मवनं विलग्नं सरोजिनीपत्रमिवोढपंकम् ॥ ३६ ॥
items.tr:
daṃṣṭrāgravinyastamaśṣometadbhūmaṇḍalaṃ nātha vibhāvyate te |
vigāhataḥ padmavanaṃ vilagnaṃ sarojinīpatramivoḍhapaṃkam || 36 ||

items.text:
द्यावापृथिव्योरतुलप्रभाव यदन्तरं तद्वपुषा तवैव ।
व्याप्तं जगद्व्याप्तिसमर्थदीप्ते हिताय विश्वस्य विभो भव त्वम् ॥ ३७ ॥
items.tr:
dyāvāpṛthivyoratulaprabhāva yadantaraṃ tadvapuṣā tavaiva |
vyāptaṃ jagadvyāptisamarthadīpte hitāya viśvasya vibho bhava tvam || 37 ||

items.text:
परमार्थस्त्वमेवैको नान्योस्ति जगतः पते ।
तवैष महिमा येन व्याप्तमेतच्चराचरम् ॥ ३८ ॥
items.tr:
paramārthastvamevaiko nānyosti jagataḥ pate |
tavaiṣa mahimā yena vyāptametaccarācaram || 38 ||

items.text:
यदेतदृश्यते मूर्त्तमेतज्ज्ञानात्मनस्तव ।
भ्रान्तिज्ञानेन पश्यन्ति जगद्रू पमयोगिनः ॥ ३९ ॥
items.tr:
yadetadṛśyate mūrttametajjñānātmanastava |
bhrāntijñānena paśyanti jagadrū pamayoginaḥ || 39 ||

items.text:
ज्ञानस्वरूपमखिलं जगदेतदबुद्धयः ।
अर्थस्वरूपं पश्यन्तो भ्राम्यन्ते मोहसंप्लवे ॥ ४० ॥
items.tr:
jñānasvarūpamakhilaṃ jagadetadabuddhayaḥ |
arthasvarūpaṃ paśyanto bhrāmyante mohasaṃplave || 40 ||

items.text:
ये तु ज्ञानविदः शुद्धचेतसस्तेऽखिलं जगत् ।
ज्ञानात्मकं प्रपश्यन्ति त्वद्रू पं परमेश्वर ॥ ४१ ॥
items.tr:
ye tu jñānavidaḥ śuddhacetasaste'khilaṃ jagat |
jñānātmakaṃ prapaśyanti tvadrū paṃ parameśvara || 41 ||

items.text:
प्रसीद सर्व सर्वात्मन्भवाय जगतामिमाम् ।
उद्धरोर्वीममेयात्मञ्छन्नो देह्यब्जलोचन ॥ ४२ ॥
items.tr:
prasīda sarva sarvātmanbhavāya jagatāmimām |
uddharorvīmameyātmañchanno dehyabjalocana || 42 ||

items.text:
सत्त्वोद्रि क्तोऽसि भगवन् गोविंद पृथिवीमिमाम् ।
समुद्धर भवायेश शन्नो देह्यब्जलोचन ॥ ४३ ॥
items.tr:
sattvodri kto'si bhagavan goviṃda pṛthivīmimām |
samuddhara bhavāyeśa śanno dehyabjalocana || 43 ||

items.text:
सर्गप्रवृत्तिर्भवतो जगतामुपकारिणी ।
भवत्वेषा नमस्तेऽस्तु शन्नो देह्यब्जलोचन ॥ ४४ ॥
items.tr:
sargapravṛttirbhavato jagatāmupakāriṇī |
bhavatveṣā namaste'stu śanno dehyabjalocana || 44 ||

items.speaker: श्रीपराशर उवाच
items.text:
एवं संस्तूयमानस्तु परमात्मा महीधरः ।
उज्जहार क्षितिं क्षिप्रं न्यस्तवांश्च महाम्भसि ॥ ४५ ॥
items.tr:
evaṃ saṃstūyamānastu paramātmā mahīdharaḥ |
ujjahāra kṣitiṃ kṣipraṃ nyastavāṃśca mahāmbhasi || 45 ||

items.text:
तस्योपरि जलौघस्य महती नौरिव स्थिता ।
विततत्त्वात्तु देहस्य न मही याति संप्लवम् ॥ ४६ ॥
items.tr:
tasyopari jalaughasya mahatī nauriva sthitā |
vitatattvāttu dehasya na mahī yāti saṃplavam || 46 ||

items.text:
ततः क्षितिं समां कृत्वा पृथिव्यां सोचिनोद्गिरीन् ।
यथाविभागं भगवाननादिः परमेश्वरः ॥ ४७ ॥
items.tr:
tataḥ kṣitiṃ samāṃ kṛtvā pṛthivyāṃ socinodgirīn |
yathāvibhāgaṃ bhagavānanādiḥ parameśvaraḥ || 47 ||

items.text:
प्राक्यसर्गदग्धानखिलान्पर्वतान्पृथिवीतले ।
अमोघेन प्रभावेण ससर्जामोघवाञ्छितः ॥ ४८ ॥
items.tr:
prākyasargadagdhānakhilānparvatānpṛthivītale |
amoghena prabhāveṇa sasarjāmoghavāñchitaḥ || 48 ||

items.text:
भूविभागं ततः कृत्वा सप्तद्वीपान्यथातथम् ।
भूराद्यांश्चतुरो लोकान्पूर्ववत्समकल्पयत् ॥ ४९ ॥
items.tr:
bhūvibhāgaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā saptadvīpānyathātatham |
bhūrādyāṃścaturo lokānpūrvavatsamakalpayat || 49 ||

items.text:
ब्रह्मरूपधरो देवस्ततोऽसौ रजसा वृतः ।
चकार सृष्टिं भगवांश्चतुर्वक्त्रधरो हरिः ॥ ५० ॥
items.tr:
brahmarūpadharo devastato'sau rajasā vṛtaḥ |
cakāra sṛṣṭiṃ bhagavāṃścaturvaktradharo hariḥ || 50 ||

items.text:
निमित्तमात्रमेवाऽसौ सृज्यानां सर्गकर्मणि ।
प्रधानकारणीभूता यतो वै सृज्यशक्तयः ॥ ५१ ॥
items.tr:
nimittamātramevā'sau sṛjyānāṃ sargakarmaṇi |
pradhānakāraṇībhūtā yato vai sṛjyaśaktayaḥ || 51 ||

items.text:
निमित्तमात्रं मुक्त्वैवं नान्यत्किंचिदपेक्षते ।
नीयते तपतां श्रेष्ठ स्वशक्त्या वस्तु वस्तुताम् ॥ ५२ ॥
items.tr:
nimittamātraṃ muktvaivaṃ nānyatkiṃcidapekṣate |
nīyate tapatāṃ śreṣṭha svaśaktyā vastu vastutām || 52 ||

en_chapter: Maitreya said:—"O mighty ascetic, relate unto me how the reverend Brahmā whose name is Nārāyana, created all beings at the commencement of the Kalpa". (Thereat) Parāçara said,—"Hear as to how that god, the lord of Prajāpati, the reverend Brahmā instinct with Nārāyana, created beings. On the expiration of the past Kalpa, that Master, Brahmā, surcharged with the energy of righteousness, awaking from his slumbers, saw the universe—void of all. And the supreme, incomprehensible Nārāyana—the lord of the greatest—as the worshipful Brahmā, became engaged in creation. This sloka is used with reference to the divine Nārāyana, the creator of the universe, in the form of Brahmā. Apa is named nāra, having been created by Nara; and in days of yore, (water) having been the abode of him, he hath hence been called Nārāyana.—And on the universe becoming one ocean, the creator of all beings, the Lord resting on water, inferring that the Earth was thus placed, set his heart on delivering her. And as he, on former occasions, had assumed the forms of a fish, a Tortoise, etc., he now assumed the form of a Boar. And for sustaining the entire universe, the lord of creatures, impregnated with the Veda and sacrifices, of serene soul and the soul of all,—the Supreme spirit—stay of soul, and the prop of the Earth,—hymned by the Siddhas inhabiting the region of Jana,—Sauaka and others,—then entered water.—And seeing him enter the nether regions, that exalted one, the Earth, bowing low in humility and reverence, began to praise him. And the Earth said,—'I bow unto thee, who art all being; I bow unto thee, holding the conch and the mace. Do thou rescue me from here, now, as, thou hadst formerly done. I had formerly been delivered by thee. O Janārddana, I as well as other things, such as the sky, etc., are permeated by thee. Reverence unto thee, O prime spirit, O male soul, I bow unto thee. I bow unto thee, who art pradhāna and vaykta, and who art Time. Thou, wearing the forms of Brahmā, Vishnu and Rudra, art the creator of all beings, and thou art the maintainer as well as the destroyer thereof. Having destroyed everything, thou, O Govinda, on the universe having become one Ocean,—contemplated by the pious, reposest (on the serpent-couch). None knoweth the high mystery encompassing thee; and the deities do but adore that form in which thou incarnatest thyself. O supreme Brahmā, adoring thee, those desirous of emancipation, attain the same. Who, not worshipping Vasudeva, obtaineth liberation? Thy entire form comprehends ail that may be secured by the mind, all that may be perceived by sight and the other senses, all that may be discriminated by thought. And I am supported, and created, and maintained by thee. And for this it is that people call me Mādhavi. Victory to thee, O thou that art all knowledge! Victory to thee, who art gross and undeteriorating! Victory to thee, O thou that art infinite! Victory to thee, thou that art the Nascent! Victory to thee, thou that art Manifest. Thou, O lord! O prime of prime souls! O soul of the Universe! Victory to thee, O master of sacrifice, thou, who art sinless! Thou art Sacrifice, and Vaskatkāra and thou, Omkarāa and thou, Fire. Thou art the Vedas, and thou the branches thereof, and thou Hari, art the person presiding; over sacrifice. Thou art the Sun, etc., and the planets and stars, and thou the entire universe. And O foremost god, thou art all that is formless and that is formed, and that is hard and, O best of male beings, all that I have mentioned and also all that I have left un mentioned. I bow down unto thee. I bow unto thee again and again.'"

Parāçara said:—Thus eulogised by Earth, that graceful one, the holder thereof, began to roar in Sāma accents. Then heaving up the Earth with his razors from the deep, the mighty Boar, having eyes resembling blown lotuses,—and himself like unto lotus-leaves,—rose up like a gigantic dark-blue mountain. And as he emerged, the troubled water dashed by the wind forced out from his mouth, surging up, splashed the highly resplendent and sinless ascetics, Sananda and others, dwellers of the regions of Jana. And on the nether regions being broken up by the hoof-impacts (of the boar), the water began to run down with roars; and the Siddhas constantly inhabiting the regions of Jana, were moved about by the air of his breath. And the ascetics, placed in the tactual pores of the mighty bore as he rose up holding the Earth in his abdominal cavity and kept shaking his Veda-impregnated person,—experienced the highest bliss. And yogis dwelling in the regions of Jana, Sananda and others, with delighted hearts, and with heads bent in humility, hymned the holder of the Earth, remaining moveless, with his eyes expanded,—saying,—"Victory unto thee, O foremost God of gods,—O Keçava, O wielder of the conch, mace, sword and discus! The cause of creation, destruction and sustentation, save thee, supreme state there is none whatever. The Vedas are thy feet, and the yupa, thy larger tooth, and Sacrifice, thy smaller; the place of the (sacrificial fire) is thy mouth, and the fire itself thy tongue; and darva is thy down. O Lord, thou art the person presiding over Sacrifice. O mighty soul, day and night are thy eyes; and that refuge of all—the state of Brahmā, himself—is thy head; the entire complement of Suktas composeth thy matted locks; and thy tongue is the sacrificial offerings, O god. O thou having the (sacrificial) ladle for thy face! O thou who hast the solemn accents of Sāma for thy voice, O thou that hast the front-part of the sacrificial ground, for thy body! O thou who hast all the sacrifices for thy joints! O god, thou hast for thy ears the morality of the Smritis as well as the Srutis. Be thou propitiated! O undeteriorating one, O thou that hast the Universe for thy form, we know thee as having covered the Earth with thy paces, and that thou art the cause and stay thereof. Thou art the foremost Lord of the cosmos. Be thou gracious! Thou art the master of the mobile and the immobile. Raised on thy razor-ends, all this Earth, O Lord, seemeth like a lotus-leaf besmeared with mud on the tusk of an elephant that hath plunged into a pool of lotuses. O thou of unparalleled power, all the space between heaven and earth hath been covered with thy body. O thou, the universe hath been enveloped with whose splendour, O Lord, prove thou of profit to the universe. Thou art the sole highest reality,—there is none other, sovereign of the universe. And this glory in which the mobile and the immobile are enfolded,—is thine. O thou that art knowledge, unspiritual people, through ignorance, look upon this form of thine displayed in the world. Foolish persons, regarding this entire universe impregnated with knowledge, as real, fall into a sea of delusion. But O supreme lord, those that are versed in knowledge and are of pure spirit, look on this entire universe as thy form replete with knowledge. O Sarva, O soul of all! Be thou gracious! For the good of this world do thou, O thou of immeasurable soul, raise the Earth up. O lotus-eyed one, confer on us what is good. Thou, O reverend one, art surcharged with the virtue of goodness. O Govinda, for the benefit (of all), O lord, raise up this Earth. O lotus-eyed one, confer on us what is good. Mayst thou incline thy mind to creation fraught with profit to the universe! We bow unto thee. O lotus-eyed one, confer on us what is good".

Parāçara said,—"Thus hymned by the divinities, that supreme soul, the holder of Earth, at once lifted her up, and set her on the mighty sea. And, resting on the sea like a giant bark, Earth did not sink in consequence of the flatness of her frame. Then leveling the Earth, the worshipful supreme Lord without beginning, placed mountains on her in proper order. And by his infallible power, that one of truthful purposes created on the Earth all the mountains that had been burnt on the occasion of the burning of the foregone creation. And then; properly dividing the land containing seven islands, he, as formerly, created the four regions, viz., Bhuva and the rest. And then, possessed with the principle of passion, the reverend Deity, Hari, wearing the form of Brahmā and assuming four faces, set about creation, But in the matter of creation, he was an instrument merely; as the force resident in the things created, was the principal Cause. Being ripe for development, (objects at the time of creation) desiderate nothing more. O foremost of those practising austerities, objects attain their objectivity by virtue of their inherent force".
